{"task": {"id": "I_kwDONElfw88AAAABWBhjBA", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BlV6Pzg_kISg", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BlV6P", "number": 33, "title": "Implement PMX material morph playback in TSL, including groups, alpha and outlines", "body": "## Goal

Implement **PMX type 8 material morph playback** in the Three.js r186 TSL / NodeMaterial-based `three-mmd-loader`, including VMD morph tracks and direct type 0 **group → material morph** links. Ensure surfaces, texture/sphere/toon colors, alpha/transparency and MMD outlines update correctly across WebGL2 and native WebGPU.

This follows completed [#26 SDEF](https://github.com/takahirox/three-mmd-loader/issues/26), [#28 bone morph](https://github.com/takahirox/three-mmd-loader/issues/28), and [#31 group morph](https://github.com/takahirox/three-mmd-loader/issues/31).

## Current gaps

- `MMDLoader.GeometryBuilder` retains a placeholder morph target for type 8 but does not preserve a runnable material morph controller/payload.
- `MaterialBuilder.checkAlphaMorph` only flags some target materials as potentially transparent at load time. It does **not** animate material values, and its preclassification needs to account for both multiplication/addition modes and the special material index `-1` (all materials).
- `MMDToonMaterial` is a TSL `MeshPhongNodeMaterial` using MMD toon lighting, map/matcap and derived emissive/ambient properties. `MMDOutlineEffect` owns a separate inverted-hull outline pass whose thickness/color/alpha must reflect morphs.
- Current group evaluation supports type 1 vertices and type 2 bones, but ignores type 8 targets.

## Implementation scope

1. **Preserve type 8 metadata.** Load type 8 morph name/index and all per-element properties already parsed by `mmd-parser ^1.1.4`: material index, calculation mode (multiply/add), diffuse RGBA, specular RGB, shininess, ambient RGB, edge RGBA/size, and texture / sphere-map / toon RGBA. Preserve public `morphTargetDictionary` / `morphTargetInfluences`, including PMD and unsupported morph compatibility. Invalid target indices/modes must not crash rendering.
2. **Evaluate weights deterministically.** For each material, start from its original immutable PMX-derived parameters every update. Apply direct material morph weights plus contributions from every direct type 0 group reference `groupWeight × elementRatio`, with existing MMD policy to ignore group→group links. Multiple affected materials, multiple morphs on one material, duplicate references, negative/zero/noninteger/nonfinite invalid inputs, non-clamped effective group weights, and material index `-1` must be handled/documented. Preserve PMX morph and element order rather than incidental UI order.
3. **Correct PMX material morph arithmetic.** The weighted multiplication coefficient for component `v` is `1 + (v - 1) * weight`; weighted addition is `delta * weight`. Apply to each specified channel as appropriate, including RGBA and edge size. Exercise both types, weight `0/0.5/1`, additive/multiplicative interactions, restoration, and full-material targeting against an independent reference. Do not introduce coordinate-space flips for material data.
4. **Map onto TSL materials faithfully.** Update visible diffuse, specular, shininess, ambient/emissive, alpha, and base/map/sphere/toon color multipliers using the MMD/Three color-space conventions and existing texture/toon/material setup. Preserve the existing 0.2 ambient scaling when a diffuse map is present. Handle PMX texture, sphere and toon morph color factors in shader-based TSL (not by modifying shared texture contents). Avoid mutating textures shared across materials.
5. **Transparency and outlines.** Support materials originally opaque that morph to partially/fully transparent, both multiplication and addition, and `index:-1`; preserve correct blending/depth/side classification and texture alpha. Ensure `MMDOutlineEffect` updates derived edge color, edge alpha and thickness, including visibility when edge size reaches zero. Avoid needless shader recompiles or material churn each frame. Document/render-test relevant transparency sorting and shadow-pass behavior.
6. **Integrate with existing animation helper.** Reuse `mesh.morphTargetInfluences` and VMD morph tracks. Direct slider updates via `helper.update(0)`, active/paused playback, seek, loop, reset, stop, helper transfer, and `pmxAnimation: true` must avoid cumulative drift. Existing bone/group/vertex morph animation, SDEF and IK/grant/physics behavior must stay intact. Expose a documented feature toggle or equivalent controllable semantics if necessary; avoid extending user-facing API gratuitously.
7. **Scope boundaries.** UV/additional-UV morphs, PMX 2.1 flip/impulse morphs, additional sphere envFlag 3 support and full Grant work are separate tasks. Material morph support must not silently claim those features are now implemented. Do not change existing public example models/motions/screenshots, published asset list or Pages URLs.

## Optional, private real-model inspection

- Extend the existing **loopback-only** `npm run dev:sdef` private viewer (or add an equally isolated viewer) with a `material-morph/` source option, a list of the actual parsed type 8 material morphs and referenced materials, a direct/group weight slider, and material parameter/outline diagnostics. Include a clear warning when a candidate PMX has no type 8 morph.
- **YYB式初音ミク 10th v1.02** (original distribution https://bowlroll.net/file/146083) is a possible local candidate for material/alpha effects since it is already a planned SDEF model, but actual type 8 payloads and usable target morph names **must be verified from the obtained PMX**. If inadequate, identify a separately licensed model; do not invent or assume verified material morphs.
- Require legitimate manual acquisition and review of the actual archive README/license **only for optional human inspection**. Keep PMX, VMD, textures and licenses in Git-ignored `examples/assets/private/material-morph/`; no automatic downloads, Git commits, npm bundles, Actions artifacts, Pages uploads or public redistribution of third-party assets. Existing private SDEF, bone and group viewers remain functional.
- Visual inspection is **not** a merge gate; keep deferred checks separate from already-completed implementation issues. See [#30](https://github.com/takahirox/three-mmd-loader/issues/30) for the earlier optional real-model checks.

## Fully automated pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] Generate PMX fixture(s) parsed with published `mmd-parser ^1.1.4` that exercise type 8 multiply/add, full target `-1`, per-material targeting, all channel payloads, shared textures/materials, and group→material links with nontrivial ratios. Preserve the original morph dictionary/indices.
- [ ] Independently calculate expected material parameters from immutable bases for 0, 0.5, 1, combined morphs, mixed add/multiply order, multiple group contributions and return to zero; assert against runtime results without duplicating production math in tests.
- [ ] Verify initial PMX material values, diffuse RGBA, specular/shininess, ambient/emissive and its texture-dependent factor, texture/sphere/toon RGBA multipliers, edge color/size, and `-1` all-material targeting. Ensure missing textures and shared textures remain safe.
- [ ] Material alpha and outline transitions from opaque→translucent→opaque, fully transparent states, additive/multiply and group-driven transitions are correctly rendered. Assert no stray opacity/sorting/outline artifacts or persistent mutation after reset; document renderer limitations where relevant.
- [ ] Test interactive `morphTargetInfluences` changes, named VMD morph tracks and groups, paused/stop/restart/seek/loop, repeat `update(0)`, helper transfer and `pmxAnimation: true`, with stable no-drift results and preserved public weights.
- [ ] Existing PMD, vertex/bone/group morph, SDEF, IK/Grant/physics, toon/material and package consumers remain regression-safe.
- [ ] Actual TSL browser render tests assert measurable surface RGBA/color/alpha, toon/sphere/base-map color influences and outline width/color on **mandatory WebGL2** and native WebGPU **when an adapter is available**, with independent expected results; merely compiling shaders is insufficient.
- [ ] Viewer displays actual PMX type 8 morph and material diagnostics and can vary weights without packaged third-party assets. Generated fixtures suffice for CI. Private paths stay loopback-only, traversal/symlink-safe and excluded from `npm pack`, `npm run build:examples`, Pages/public assets and published URLs.
- [ ] Before merge, `npm run typecheck`, `npm test`, `npm run test:browser`, `npm run build:examples`, `npm run test:examples` and isolated npm JS/TS consumer tests pass.
- [ ] The issue can be completed using **only automated pre-merge checks**; no human visual review, model download, credentialed access, license-dependent asset or post-merge verification is required.

## Required post-merge verification

**None** for implementation Issue/PR completion. Any later hands-on PMX verification is optional and separate.

## Parser dependency

`mmd-parser@1.1.4` already exposes type 8 material morph elements with the necessary fields. **No new parser Issue or npm release is expected**, unless implementation reveals a reproducible parser defect.

## References

- [Current MMDToonMaterial](https://github.com/takahirox/three-mmd-loader/blob/main/src/materials/MMDToonMaterial.ts)
- [Current material builder / alpha classification](https://github.com/takahirox/three-mmd-loader/blob/main/src/loaders/MMDLoader.ts)
- [MMDOutlineEffect](https://github.com/takahirox/three-mmd-loader/blob/main/src/effects/MMDOutlineEffect.ts)
- [Group morph behavior](https://github.com/takahirox/three-mmd-loader/blob/main/docs/group-morphs.md)
